title.value: Limitations of Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for Gradient Descent Methods in Stochastic Convex Optimization
title.justification: The title is stated at the beginning of the paper and in various sections, highlighting the focus of the paper on the limitations of information-theoretic generalization bounds.
title.quote: Limitations of Information-Theoretic Generalization Bounds for Gradient Descent Methods in Stochastic Convex Optimization

analysis.description: This paper critically analyzes the applicability of information-theoretic frameworks to establish generalization bounds for gradient descent methods within stochastic convex optimization. It demonstrates the limitations of such bounds to achieve minimax rates, even with the introduction of Gaussian noise as a surrogate algorithm, and identifies gaps in existing techniques that highlight the need for developing new analytical tools for this purpose.

type.justification: The paper provides a theoretical exploration of information-theoretic bounds and their inadequacies for capturing generalization rates in certain optimization scenarios, lacking experimental or empirical results.
type.quote: In this work, we uncover limitations of information-theoretic techniques towards analyzing stochastic gradient descent.
